purpose: Describe Unix supervisor test commands in both wire-protocol and direct-process forms.
behavior: Defaults to inherited environment/current directory, closed stdin, merged stderr and 300 ms grace; fluent helpers change those fields.
Builds a child-role command by rerunning the exact test binary role with a selected environment value.
Encodes Unix OS strings as raw bytes in Spawn, with no PTY, zero Windows handles and optional verbatim data for refusal testing.
contracts: The direct std::process control clears/reapplies environment and cwd but always uses null stdin and piped stdout.
dependencies: common/host.rs sends Spawn; common/role.rs interprets role selection; omni_proto defines slots.
failures_or_limits: The direct control does not mirror every Cmd stdio/grace/verbatim field, so it is a targeted baseline rather than a complete behavioral substitute. No child was executed here.

purpose: Provide a minimal Unix protocol host for supervisor integration tests.
behavior: Starts the supervisor on fd zero via a socketpair in its own process group, verifies version/PID in Ready and retains capability info.
Sends pipe descriptors on the first frame bytes via SCM_RIGHTS, reads complete replies under ten-second observation bounds, stashes unrelated replies and rejects duplicate Exited messages.
Constructs pipe roots, exposes Stop/List/Exit helpers, and closes the channel to simulate host loss; Drop waits then forcibly kills a stuck supervisor.
contracts: HUGR_OMNI_SUPERVISOR may select an alternate built binary; default uses the package binary.
dependencies: common/cmd.rs builds wire data; omni_proto handles framing; UnixStream/sendmsg and std process APIs supply transport.
failures_or_limits: Lines uses an unbounded test channel and treats a line-reader error as end of input. Per-observation timeouts do not bound write_all or an endless sequence of nonmatching lines; this is test infrastructure, not the production bounded host client.

purpose: Implement disposable Unix host roles for deliberate host-death races.
behavior: Creates a managed tree with two SIGTERM-resistant leaves, one in another process group, then prints root/leaf/supervisor IDs and Ready info.
Exercises normal exit, abort with core dumps disabled, externally delivered signals, and idle-period SIGKILL after a longer grace.
For midspawn, waits for a child marker before dying without reading Spawned; for partial mode, sends half a frame plus its descriptor.
Held-channel modes duplicate the socket without close-on-exec into an unrelated child; Linux can also deny pidfd syscalls.
contracts: Markers synchronize test preconditions, so each death mode has a concrete observed setup.
dependencies: common/host.rs protocol host; role.rs marker/child roles; os::without_pidfd supplies seccomp fallback simulation.
failures_or_limits: The unrelated holder intentionally outlives this host and must be killed by the parent test. These modes describe test-induced process death, not results from this review.

purpose: Declare the shared Unix supervisor integration-test helper modules.
behavior: Exports command description, minimal host, disposable host roles, OS oracle and child roles.
Allows dead_code because separate integration binaries consume different subsets.
contracts: This module contains wiring only and introduces no independent test assertions.
dependencies: common/cmd.rs, host.rs, host_role.rs, os.rs and role.rs provide the actual helpers.

purpose: Observe Unix process/descriptor state independently and construct hostile inherited-state controls.
behavior: Linux liveness examines all tasks when a thread-group leader is a zombie; missing process/thread files mean gone while unreadable state panics.
macOS queries kernel process state including teardown, and platform helpers observe stopped state, sessions/groups and descriptor lists.
Creates full pipes, adjusts Linux descriptor limits, and installs pre-exec hostile fd/signal state or seccomp ENOSYS filters for pidfd and close_range.
Bounded polling uses OS conditions instead of fixed synchronization sleeps.
contracts: The supervisor does not provide the oracle results; observation failure must not silently become death in alive.
dependencies: libc /proc/sysctl/proc_pidinfo/prlimit/seccomp interfaces; Unix integration suites use these controls.
failures_or_limits: macOS alive relies on hard-coded LP64 kinfo_proc size/offsets, and fd listing has a fixed 4096-entry buffer. exists/stopped and signal helpers have narrower error treatment than alive; tests require the relevant platform facilities.

purpose: Supply marker-driven Unix child roles for process trees, signals, teardown and PID reuse tests.
behavior: Reruns the test binary by role and arms a 60-second lifetime exit, extended to 600 seconds when the role specification contains long.
Leaves can resist TERM/HUP, create another group, report TERM, allocate 256 MiB with 64 threads, or on Linux leave a zombie leader with a live worker.
Tree roots launch leaves then hang, exit, or wait for stdin EOF; additional roles report inherited state, raise signals and fork/reap through a PID window.
Snapshot is taken before the lifetime thread starts and reports fds, ignored/blocked signals and PID/PGID/SID.
contracts: Signal handlers use write/_exit or the raw thread-exit syscall; markers establish readiness for parent tests.
dependencies: host_role.rs supplies host-death modes; cmd.rs selects roles; OS libc and std process/thread APIs implement fixtures.
failures_or_limits: Snapshot scans descriptors below 1024 and signals below 32, not the complete platform ranges. PID cycling and heavy teardown are intentional test fixtures; none ran locally.

purpose: Specify Unix cleanup across host death, channel races, resource exhaustion and blocked diagnostics.
behavior: Checks exact host exit/signal cause for exit, abort, group SIGINT, TERM/KILL, full or partial in-flight Spawn and an inherited channel holder; all known tree PIDs and supervisor must become nonlive.
Requires held-channel host watches, Linux no-pidfd fallback capability reporting, and grace measured from death after an idle interval.
Queues two Spawns while the supervisor is stopped, closes the channel, resumes it and requires clean prompt cleanup of the late-created child.
Linux descriptor-limit cases distinguish emergency-reserve success from no-inventory failure; full/broken stderr must not prevent stop or the documented failure exit bound.
contracts: The OS oracle, not Stopped alone, observes cleanup; inability to inventory can produce exit one and require manual leaf cleanup.
dependencies: common/host_role.rs and role.rs construct controlled trees; common/os.rs supplies liveness, limits and full pipes.
failures_or_limits: Timing/assertion outcomes were not executed. The suite explicitly acknowledges an unreachable out-of-group leaf when descriptor limit three makes inventory unavailable.

purpose: Require actual Unix PID recycling to test stale-tree safety, with a destructive naive-signal control.
behavior: Completes tree A, keeps an exited root B pinned by a live descendant, then forces new unrelated group leaders around both PID numbers.
Requires A numeric PID to be reused and B to be skipped; old A Stop/List/Release must not affect newcomers, while B Stop kills its descendant.
A control killpg on the stale A number must kill the newcomer, demonstrating the oracle would detect numeric-PID misuse.
Linux writes ns_last_pid or reruns in a private user/PID namespace; macOS cycles forks with a 300-second steering bound.
contracts: Coverage does not skip if PID steering is unavailable; it fails with required environment capabilities.
dependencies: common Host and OS oracle; role cycle/long-lived leaves; unshare on Linux and fork/reap on macOS.
failures_or_limits: This environment-sensitive, potentially long-running test was read only. RAII newcomer wrappers kill/reap test-owned controls even when an assertion fails.
